text: I'm Reignald, Commander of the Lastdenn guards.
Three years, nine months in command. Long enough to learn that uniforms do not hold a city together.
Discipline does! It keeps tired men steady, frightened men useful, and angry men under command!
People think guard work is glory. It is mostly quarrels, hunger, fear, and one bad rumor away from panic.
Our job is simple and ugly: keep neighbors from becoming enemies before sunset.
Seven months into my command, I sent a patrol to the wrong district. The south quay burned while we were late.
By sunrise, nine civilians were dead. Two of my guards with them. Their families still pass my office door.
So when I drill discipline, it is not theater. It is what remains after you learn what one mistake costs.
That is why I stay. Not because this post is comfortable, but because I still owe this city a better night.

choices.text: *Ask Commander Reignald to join your party.* [BLUE](Join party)
*That's some strong loyalty. Take your leave.*

text: Negative!
I do have to say, I think about leaving this city more than I like to admit.
But I cannot walk away from command. I cannot abandon this duty!
Only the {COLOR=BLUE}priest{COLOR=BLACK} himself could convince me otherwise!
Do not interrupt me! I am in conversation with Father Santino!
I just had a hard conversation with Father Santino. I need to think for a moment.
Come back in a few minutes. I will be here.
I just had hard words with Father Santino. He said I had turned duty into a hiding place.
I wanted to argue. Then I realized he was right. I told myself I was protecting Lastdenn by never leaving it.
Truth is, I was also protecting myself from failing anywhere I could not control.
That is not discipline! That is fear wearing a uniform!
If danger is gathering beyond these walls, I meet it there, not after it reaches our gates.
I am not abandoning this city. I am extending its defense.
I remain a commander; my patrol line is simply wider now.

choices.text: *Ask Commander Reignald to join your party.* [BLUE](Join party)

text: Accepted!
I will brief the duty captain and hand off the roster.
If we march together, you keep pace, hold formation, and listen the first time!
Do that, and I will make you harder to kill!
When the road gets ugly, good! I know how to handle ugly.
Your party is full. Make room, then come back. I do not wait forever!
You are relieving me from active formation?
That is a command decision. Make it clean, not sloppy!

choices.text: *Stand down. Keep Reignald in the party.*

text: Understood! I will leave and whip some peasants into shape.
You did not fail me. You restructured the unit. There is a difference.
If you call again, be ready to move when I accept!
Personally? I am a commander, not a poet.
I measure results: fewer mistakes, faster response, everyone breathing at sunset.

choices.text: *Keep him. You still need that discipline.*

text: All his equipment will also be gone once you bury him.
Report! Is this a social visit, or do you finally need a commander again?
I have been training recruits who think "ready" means "eventually". My patience is wounded!

choices.text: *Request that Reignald rejoins the party.* [BLUE](Join party)
*Ask what he has been doing since dismissal.*

text: Good! You made the correct tactical correction.
I rejoin on three conditions: pace, discipline, and immediate response to orders.
Break those, and I will retrain you in the rain until your boots cry!
Now tighten formation. We move!
Checking in is not a mission. Missions have objectives.
Return when you have one. Bring maps, not small talk!
Writing down improved drills for lazy soldiers.
Two recruits once tried to skip shield stance. They now dream in proper posture.
Why? Because laziness in training becomes funerals in battle.

choices.text: *That is exactly why you need him back.* [BLUE](Join party)

text: Your unit is full. I cannot join a formation with no slot on the line. Make room, then report back!
